name: Lazarus Synthetic Personhood Hearing Formal Robe
description:
Lazarus developed this robe specifically for use by synthetic beings appearing before the GLMZ Personhood Recognition Tribunal — a garment created to satisfy the tribunal's requirement for 'appropriate formal presentation' while accommodating synthetic physiognomy, which varies widely. The robe is constructed in a clean ivory-white with Lazarus's caduceus motif rendered in pale gray at the breast — visible enough to signal institutional backing, restrained enough not to read as corporate branding in a legal context. Internal magnetic closures adjust automatically to non-standard torso configurations, and the fabric has no thermal, biometric, or BCI-reactive properties that might interfere with the tribunal's own scanning environment.

The robe is provided free of charge by Lazarus to synthetic clients entering personhood proceedings — a gesture that reads as advocacy to some and as calculated PR to others. Lazarus's interest in synthetic personhood is not purely altruistic: recognized synthetic persons become potential customers for Lazarus's cognitive maintenance and neural-substrate pharmaceutical lines. The robe is, in this light, both a gift and an investment. Synthetics in advocacy communities are aware of this tension and wear the robe anyway, because the alternative is appearing in tribunal in whatever they were wearing when they filed.
cultural_context: The Lazarus hearing robe has become a contested symbol in synthetic rights communities. Some see it as dignified institutional support; others see it as Lazarus branding synthetics before they've even been recognized as persons. Advocacy groups have produced alternative robes in neutral colors for synthetics who refuse the Lazarus version, though these alternatives lack the tribunal's informal 'appropriate presentation' precedent behind them.
story_hooks: A synthetic being refuses the Lazarus robe on principle and arrives in a Coldseam patched formal set — the tribunal panel's reaction to this choice reveals more about them than any testimony.
A Lazarus PR operative is quietly photographing synthetic clients in the white robes for an internal campaign about the corponation's 'commitment to personhood' — without consent.
A synthetic who won their personhood case still has the robe; they've kept it, and the choice to keep or destroy it has become a private ritual question.

physical_description.visual_profile: A floor-length formal robe with architectural simplicity — high neckline, straight vertical lines, designed to drape equally over standard and non-standard torso geometries. Projects institutional neutrality with subtle medical institutional branding. Reads as dignity rather than fashion.
physical_description.fit: Loose, non-fitted construction that accommodates synthetic bodies of variable shape — chrome limbs, distributed processing units, non-human skeletal architecture. Magnetic closures at the front adjust automatically without visible fasteners. Sleeves cut generous and straight, ending at wrist equivalent on any arm type.
physical_description.primary_material: Treated synthetic ivory-white composite — thermal-neutral, non-conductive, chosen specifically to not interfere with tribunal scanning equipment. Matte finish, professional grade.
physical_description.texture: Smooth and structured, with subtle weight — fabric has slight body and holds clean drape. No sheen or reflectivity. Close inspection reveals careful quality construction; the garment is engineered, not merely tailored.
physical_description.color_scheme: Ivory-white base with pale gray caduceus motif at left breast — medical/institutional symbolism, deliberately understated. No accent colors or patterns beyond the single branded symbol.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic snap closures running full length front, concealed behind overlap. No visible fasteners, zippers, or hardware. System auto-adjusts to wearer's specific torso geometry.
distinctive_features: Automatic magnetic closure system calibrated to synthetic physiognomy
Caduceus motif in pale gray at breast — Lazarus institutional marker
No thermal, biometric, or BCI-reactive properties to avoid tribunal scanner interference
Asymmetrically designed interior to accommodate non-standard internal architecture
Sleeves convertible for various limb configurations
Pockets integrated but invisible from exterior
Fabric treated to shed particulates and maintain pristine appearance
physical_description.tier_indicator: Provided free by Lazarus — nominally Tier 1 quality, but accessibility makes it functionally Tier 3+. Synthetics across all tiers wear it.
physical_description.cultural_context: Symbol of institutional backing in synthetic personhood proceedings, but also a point of contention — some see it as Lazarus advocacy, others as corporate branding of the legally vulnerable. Wearing it signals either trust in Lazarus or pragmatic acceptance of tribunal norms. Advocacy communities recognize the double bind: the robe increases chances of favorable tribunal presentation, but at the cost of appearing Lazarus-endorsed.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine on first tribunal appearance — the garment arrives shrink-wrapped and untouched. Subsequent wearings show careful maintenance; synthetic wearers often treat it with ceremony. Wear is minimal because the robe's life is typically brief: one or two tribunal sessions before either recognition is granted or the proceedings conclude.

image_prompt: Close-up fashion photography of an ivory-white formal hearing robe draped on a sleek chrome and composite synthetic mannequin with non-standard torso geometry—extra articulation points, visible substrate housing. The pale gray caduceus motif subtly visible at the left breast. Soft, clinical lighting from above suggesting tribunal chamber ambiance. Minimalist dark background. The robe photographed mid-drape to show its engineered structure and invisible magnetic closures. Sharp focus on fabric texture and institutional tailoring. Moody institutional color grading—cool whites, subtle grays. --ar 2:3 --v 6
